description: Apply a bulk price change — step 2 of 2, after preview_bulk_price_change. Send the SAME rule, scope and target and the digest the preview returned, copied verbatim and never invented. The plan is recomputed from live prices and refused with CONFLICT if it no longer matches the digest (prices moved, or the rule would compound on a retry) — preview again and show the person the new numbers. Changes real prices: a selling price reaches connected channels where the owner armed price writes; a purchase cost is never published. Returns { affected, skipped }. Needs the owner's "AI may change prices in bulk" switch (Settings → Integrations → Connect AI); without it the call is refused and you should tell the person to ask the owner. Not idempotent for percent rules — never repeat a successful apply. Confirm with the person unless they asked for the change outright. Echoes the workspace.

digest.description: The digest returned by preview_bulk_price_change for THIS rule, scope and target — copied verbatim, never invented. If prices moved since, the apply returns CONFLICT and you must preview again.

rule.description: HOW prices move. The target 'cost' accepts only op 'percent'. Pick the one that matches the request: a percent change, a fixed price, a markup over cost, a discount (and its end), or the old price.

op.description: Raise or lower by a percent.

percent.description: Percent change: 10 raises by 10%, -10 lowers by 10%. Between -90 and 900.

rounding.description: How the new price is rounded: cents (to 2 decimals), whole (up to the next whole unit), nine (up to the next price ending in 9, e.g. 644.80 -> 649) or tens (up to the next ten). Everything except cents rounds UP.

amount.description: One price for EVERY product in scope, as a decimal string, e.g. '1290' or '1290.50'. Rare for a whole category — check the preview.

op.description: Set one price for every product in scope.

markupPercent.description: Markup over the purchase cost, in percent: 40 means price = cost x 1.4. The cost is crossed into the price's currency at the rates the workspace states; a product without a cost or a rate is skipped.

op.description: Price = purchase cost plus a markup.

rounding.description: How the new price is rounded: cents (to 2 decimals), whole (up to the next whole unit), nine (up to the next price ending in 9, e.g. 644.80 -> 649) or tens (up to the next ten). Everything except cents rounds UP.

op.description: Start a sale: the old price becomes the current price (or stays, if a higher one is set) and the price drops by the percent.

rounding.description: How the new price is rounded: cents (to 2 decimals), whole (up to the next whole unit), nine (up to the next price ending in 9, e.g. 644.80 -> 649) or tens (up to the next ten). Everything except cents rounds UP.

op.description: End a sale: the price returns to the old price and the old price is cleared.
Set the old (struck-through) price above the current price by a percent. Does not change the price.

percent.description: How far above the price the old price sits, in percent.

rounding.description: How the new price is rounded: cents (to 2 decimals), whole (up to the next whole unit), nine (up to the next price ending in 9, e.g. 644.80 -> 649) or tens (up to the next ten). Everything except cents rounds UP.

op.description: Remove the old price. Does not change the price.

scope.description: WHICH products. Prefer a named container (category, brand, supplier, warehouse) when the person says 'all products of …' — it is read back by name in the preview. There is no free filter: a request like 'everything cheaper than 100' is not a scope; find the products first and send their ids.

ids.description: Explicit product ids actually fetched with search_products, at most 100.

kind.description: Specific products you fetched. Prefer a container.

id.description: The warehouse id returned by list_warehouses.
The category id returned by list_categories.

includeSubcategories.description: true to include every sub-category under it ('everything under Backpacks'); omit it for exactly that one category. Never widen it unless the person means the whole branch.

id.description: The brand id returned by list_brands.
The supplier id returned by list_suppliers.
The model id from get_product (its model block).

kind.description: Every article of one product model.

target.description: WHICH number moves. Omit it to change the product's own selling price. Use {field:'price', currency:'EUR'} for the euro price list, {field:'cost'} for the purchase cost.

currency.description: null (default) = the product's own price in the workspace currency. A 3-letter code = that currency's row of the product's price list (the workspace currency itself means null).

field.description: Change the purchase cost (percent only). Not published to channels.
